messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV cache memory spike observed in long-span inference pool (us-east-1). Continuous batching active shards increased x3. Auto-throttle triggered.

devon: oncall here, seeing the pager — pulling logs + metrics. can anyone confirm which model variants are hot?

raj: looks like ntk-extended + yarn sliding-window combo. kv cardinality jumped, vmem per-worker hit ~86%. a lot of requests queued into continuous batch.

elaine: confirmed. we rolled out 'context-window-extension' flag last night (small percentage). long-span requests amplify key prefixes.

devon: ok, immediate mitigations i want to try: 1) disable sliding-window for long-span routes 2) reduce continuous_batch.max_inflight to 64 3) set kv.eviction_age_secs=60 for affected pools. applying 1 now.

raj: +1, disabling sliding-window on route /v1/generate/long-span. making infra hotpatch.

deploy-bot: hotpatch applied to 6 hosts in pool longspan-alpha. change_id=chg_20260315_01

devon: applying reduced inflight and kv-eviction now. config snippet i'm pushing: 

```
continuous_batch:
  max_inflight: 64
kv_cache:
  eviction_age_secs: 60
  max_entries_per_shard: 200000
```

maria: i see tail latency dropping but some upstream 502/504s persist. customers 8204 and 9182 reported 504s via support.

elaine: recommend fallback to compact model variant (ntk-lite) for requests queued >5s. cheaper KV footprint, lower memory pressure. can we route slow-queued requests to ntk-lite?

raj: added routing rule: slow_queue -> model:ntk-lite in traffic-router v2. smoke-testing now.

devon: smoke tests look good. memory usage trending down from ~86% to ~58% over 10m after patches. throughput normalizing.

maria: customer comms: sent interim note to 8204/9182. no data loss, we observed elevated 5xxs for ~12m. created tickets INC-3781 and INC-3782.

devon: marking incident severity SEV2 (partial service degradation). handing off to maria for monitoring and post-incident follow-up. handoff summary:
- root cause: interaction between context-window-extension flag and YaRN sliding-window leading to high KV key diversity on long-span workloads
- mitigations applied: sliding-window disabled; continuous_batch.max_inflight reduced; kv eviction aggressive; fallback routing to ntk-lite variant
- impact: elevated 5xxs for ~12m, two customer reports, no PII exposure
- follow-ups: revert context-extension rollout; add canary for high-cardinality workloads; implement auto-kv-throttle heuristic; longer-term: per-route kv sharding improvements

maria: taking handoff. will monitor until 1000 UTC. follow-up owners: raj (runtime RCA), elaine (rollback + rollout guard), devon (postmortem draft). ping me if any regressions. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: oncall handoff recorded. next_oncall=maria. incident_state=monitoring.

devon: thanks team. i'll collect timeline and perf graphs. metrics dashboard: https://metrics.internal/redwood/incident/1832501234

raj: saved a preliminary note to /runbooks/long-span-kv-cardinality.md with replication steps and logs. will expand with exact traces.

maria: starting postmortem template and severity review. assigning owners for action items.

elaine: i'll coordinate rollback of the context-extension flag and add an automated guard so context-extension + sliding-window can't be enabled together.

devon: closing pager for now. will re-open if anything spikes. :eyes:
